intro: WELCOME. This is a realistic-opponent repertoire for WHITE built around the Italian Opening — the oldest and still one of the best ways to play after 1.e4 e5. White develops with Nf3 and Bc4, keeps the centre flexible with d3 and c3, and then manoeuvres: the b1-knight travels to g3, the rook comes to e1, and the break d4 is prepared before it is played. There is no forced theory to memorise and no position where White is simply worse — the Italian wins by accumulating small advantages and then attacking. Built the same way as the companion Sicilian, Queen's Gambit, Indian Defenses, English Opening, King's Indian Attack, London System, Colle System and King's Indian Defense encyclopedias: main plans, common tries you'll actually meet, sharp lines, typical mistakes, every line verified move-by-move for legality. PLANNED TABLE OF CONTENTS — Chapter 1: Understanding the Italian (the slow build-up, the c4-bishop, choosing the centre, the knight manoeuvre, the kingside build-up, and when the opening does not apply). Chapter 2: The Giuoco Pianissimo (3...Bc5 4.d3 and the main tabiya). Chapter 3: The Giuoco Piano with 4.c3. Chapter 4: The Two Knights Defence. Chapter 5: The Evans Gambit. Chapter 6: Black's Other Third Moves. Chapter 7: Attacking Plans and Typical Middlegames. Chapter 8: Traps and Tactics Compendium. Every line is completed to fifteen moves for each side with engine-verified top play, and every coach comment is preserved.
